# Model assumptions

**Source of truth:** `results/numbers.json` (regenerated by `python -m src.make_all`). Any number below that conflicts with `numbers.json` is stale; the JSON wins. Parameter values are quoted from the module defaults named in each section; where the code states a source it is cited as written there, otherwise the value is an engineering assumption (see the paper's assumptions table).

Package version 1.3.0 (`pyproject.toml`); log updated 21 August 2026. Module 7400MENR MSc dissertation, Liverpool John Moores University.

## 4. PV conversion chain (`src/pv_model.py`)

| Item | Value | Basis stated in code |
|---|---|---|
| Orientation | tilt = site latitude, azimuth 180° (south) | rule of thumb for year-round off-grid use; a latitude + 15° tilt reduces annual yield by 6.9% (Southampton) and 7.4% (Edinburgh) while raising December yield by 3.7% and 5.6% (`numbers.json` -> `tilt_plus15`) |
| Transposition | Hay-Davies from GHI, DNI, DHI with extraterrestrial DNI; ground albedo 0.20 (the PVGIS value) | pvlib `get_total_irradiance`, `ALBEDO` in `src/pv_model.py` |
| Incidence-angle losses | physical IAM on the beam component (n = 1.526, K = 4, L = 2 mm); Marion integrated IAM for sky-diffuse and ground-reflected components | as in PVWatts v5 |
| Cell temperature | SAPM, open-rack glass-glass (a = -3.47, b = -0.0594, deltaT = 3) | pvlib `sapm_cell` |
| DC power | PVWatts DC, temperature coefficient -0.35%/°C | typical mono-Si |
| Loss chain | see below; multiplicative derate 0.8726 (12.7% total) applied to the DC output at the battery bus | PVWatts v5 loss framework (Dobos, NREL/TP-6A20-62641, 2014) |
| Degradation | 0.5%/yr central; 0.3, 0.8 and 1.0%/yr in the sensitivity (1.0%/yr for UK field evidence, Dhimish 2020); 0.8%/yr in the worst case | `src/sizing.py`, `src/sensitivity.py` |

| Loss | Value | Basis stated in code |
|---|---|---|
| Soiling | 2.0% | PVWatts default; UK rain-washed |
| Shading | 0.0% | open-site design requirement; horizon effect quantified separately (Section 12) |
| Snow | 0.5% | brief UK lowland events |
| Mismatch | 2.0% | PVWatts default |
| Wiring | 2.0% | PVWatts default |
| Connections | 0.5% | PVWatts default |
| Light-induced degradation | 1.5% | PVWatts default |
| Nameplate | 1.0% | PVWatts default |
| Availability | 1.0% | unattended DC system, no grid-tied inverter trips (PVWatts default is 3%) |
| MPPT charge-controller efficiency | 97% | weighted efficiency (Victron SmartSolar 75/15 datasheet: 98% peak) |
| Total | 12.7% (derate 0.8726) | |

## 5. Battery (`src/battery.py`, `src/simulation.py`)

| Parameter | Value | Basis stated in code |
|---|---|---|
| Chemistry | LFP | dominant stationary chemistry per BNEF 2025 |
| Round-trip efficiency | 92%, split as sqrt(0.92) on charge and on discharge | includes converter losses |
| Maximum depth of discharge | 80% (SoC floor at 20% of the SoH-reduced capacity) | engineering assumption |
| Self-discharge | 2% per month, applied hourly as 2%/720 | engineering assumption |
| End-of-life state of health | 80% of nameplate (governing-year condition) | `DEFAULT_BATTERY_EOL_SOH` |
| Service life | 12 years (replaced at years 12 and 24); 8, 10, 15 years in the sensitivity; {8, 10, 12, 15} in the Monte Carlo | stationary LFP calendar-life range at low C-rate (about 0.015C) |
| Cycle life (informational) | 5,000 cycles to 80% | not used in the simulation |
| Initial state of charge | 50% (of nameplate, capped at the SoH ceiling, in `run_simulation`; of the SoH-reduced capacity in `multiyear.simulate_multiyear`); every reported run is a second pass that starts from the first pass's final SoC, which removes the start-condition bias | `run_simulation`, `simulate_multiyear` |
| Cold-charge option | charging can be blocked when ambient <= 0 °C (`charge_temp_limit_c`); not part of the design criterion, used only for the bounds in Section 13 | conservative proxy for the LFP low-temperature charging restriction |

## 6. Hourly simulation (`src/simulation.py`, `src/multiyear.py`)

Energy bucket at 1 h resolution: self-discharge first, then surplus PV charges the battery up to the SoH-reduced ceiling (excess is curtailed) and deficits discharge it down to the DoD floor (the remainder is unmet load). LOLP = hours with unmet load / hours simulated; EENS = unmet energy. `multiyear._bucket_loop` implements the same logic for the sixteen-year runs and is checked against `run_simulation` in the tests.

| Criterion | LOLP <= 1% in the design-governing year |

## 8. Diesel comparator (`src/diesel.py`)

Common to both architectures: 2 kVA-class air-cooled diesel set rated 1.6 kW at 0.8 power factor (no ~1 kW diesel set is sold; the smallest common sets are 2 kVA class, e.g. Yanmar YDG2700N, Hatz 1B-engined sets). Fuel from the Skarstein and Uhlen (1989) linear part-load model F [L/h] = 0.08415 x P_rated [kW] + 0.246 x P_out [kW]; the code notes that a datasheet cross-check (Onan QD3200) suggests this understates small-set consumption by roughly 25 to 50%, which is conservative for the comparison. Red diesel 76.02 p/L excluding VAT (AHDB, 2025 mean). Emission factor 2.75766 kg CO2e/L (DESNZ GHG conversion factors 2025, gas oil, Scope 1). Site visits 12 per year at £80 fuel delivery + £120 inspection = £200 per visit (paper Section III-E: about three hours of technician time at £45 to £60/h plus 90 miles at the HMRC 55p/mile rate; below the ~£250 UK contractors quote for a one-off small-genset service). Oil change £25 (engineering assumption).

| Parameter | A1: continuous | A2: battery-buffered |
|---|---|---|
| Capex | genset £2,200 (assumption; a 4.8 kVA Pramac P6000 lists at £3,453 ex VAT, 2026) + 200 L bunded tank £350 + enclosure £800 + installation £500 + AC-DC converter £80 = £3,930 | genset £2,200 + tank £350 + enclosure £800 + installation £500 + 200 Ah / 12 V lead-acid buffer £400 (about 2.4 kWh nominal, sized so that the 480 W bulk charge is C/5) + charge controller £100 + automatic start/stop controller £250 (assumption; small AMF/auto-start modules retail at £150 to £400) = £4,600 |
| Operating point | 14.64 W on 1.6 kW = 0.9% of rating, 24 h/day, 8,760 h/yr | 30% of rating (480 W, manufacturer minimum-load regime: Kubota/Caterpillar/Cummins 30%, Hatz 25%, Hatz-E/Onan 15%) |
| Runtime | 24 h/day | derived from the energy balance: 351.36 Wh/day / 0.80 lead-acid path efficiency / 480 W = 0.915 h/day, 334 h/yr |
| Fuel | 0.1382 L/h, 1,211 L/yr, £921/yr | 0.2527 L/h, 84.4 L/yr, £64/yr |
| Oil changes | every 100 h (wet stacking): 87.6 per year, £2,190/yr | every 250 h or 12 months, whichever first (Hatz 1B / Onan QD manuals): 334/250 = 1.34 per year, £33/yr |
| Genset life | 5,000 h derated life under sustained low load (NFPA 110 / Hamilton et al.; 10,000 to 30,000 h at proper load): 0.57 yr, replacement annualised | 8,000 h (assumption; no manufacturer hours-life found): 24.0 yr, so the set is replaced once, in year 24, lumpy with salvage; a 5,000 h life would add 1.9% to the A2 lifetime cost and a 10-year calendar cap 4.4% (`numbers.json` -> `diesel_life_5000h`, `diesel_calendar_life`) |
| Buffer battery | none | lead-acid, 4-year life, lumpy replacement with salvage |
| Site visits | 12/yr, £2,400/yr | 12/yr, £2,400/yr |
| CO2e | 3,340 kg/yr, 83.5 t over 25 years | 233 kg/yr, 5.8 t over 25 years |

A2 is the central comparator; A1 is the upper bound.

## 11. Carbon values (`src/dump_numbers.py`)

DESNZ central carbon values £264/t (2026) and £280/t (2030), 2020 prices, recorded in `numbers.json` -> `carbon` for the paper's discussion; not part of the LCOE.

## 12. Validation method (`src/validation.py`, `results/validation.json`)

Both layers compare DC output per kWp with PVGIS system losses set to zero and this study's loss chain switched off, so only the physics is compared. Metrics: normalised mean bias error (NMBE) and normalised RMSE, normalised by the mean of the PVGIS series over the compared samples (convention of Deville et al., 2024).

- Layer 1, same inputs, 2005-2020 hourly: PVGIS Gb(i), Gd(i), Gr(i), T2m and WS10m are fed to this study's IAM, SAPM and PVWatts steps and compared with PVGIS's own P (Huld power model, Faiman module temperature, Martin-Ruiz reflectance). Hourly NMBE +2.2, +2.9, +2.7, +2.9% and NRMSE 3.9, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7% (Southampton, Birmingham, Liverpool, Edinburgh); the bias sits in the low-irradiance classes (study / PVGIS energy ratio 1.39 to 1.41 below 100 W/m² and 1.11 between 100 and 200 W/m²) while the classes above 400 W/m², which carry 65 to 72% of the PVGIS energy, agree within 1.2%.
- Layer 2, TMY chain (Hay-Davies from GHI/DNI/DHI) against the sixteen-year PVGIS climatology by month and year: annual bias +0.6, +2.1, +2.1, +2.4%; the TMY annual yield lies inside the sixteen-year band at every site; monthly NRMSE 7.8, 15.1, 11.8, 15.4%.
- Edinburgh terrain horizon (PVGIS `usehorizon=1` against `usehorizon=0`): annual yield -0.24%, November to February -1.28%, December -1.50%.

## 13. Multi-year method and cold-weather bounds (`src/multiyear.py`, `results/multiyear.json`)

Every grid design is run through 2005-2020 under governing-year conditions with both PV models; annual LOLP, unmet hours, EENS and curtailment are recorded per year, and the cheapest design meeting each criterion is reported (`results/multiyear_grid_<site>.csv`, `results/multiyear_lolp_matrix.csv`). The step-1 TMY designs hold LOLP <= 1% in only 6, 11, 14 and 9 of the 16 years under the `study` chain (2, 5, 12 and 4 under the `pvgis` chain), which is why the final designs are adopted.

Bounds reported for the final designs (not part of the criterion): with charging blocked in every hour at or below 0 °C (162 to 437 sub-zero hours per year on the sixteen-year mean: 187, 437, 162, 430 at Southampton, Birmingham, Liverpool, Edinburgh) the designs hold LOLP <= 1% in 15, 13, 15 and 14 of the 16 years, with sixteen-year mean LOLP 0.29 to 0.84%; with a 15% winter capacity derate on top of the 80% SoH, in 16, 15, 15 and 15 years (mean LOLP 0.20 to 0.50%). Under year-1 conditions (no ageing) the final designs hold LOLP <= 1% in 16, 16, 15 and 16 years.
